title: Inside the AI software factory: Where accessibility is won or lost
partialText:
As your organization moves development into AI software factories, you must fully embed digital accessibility, just as you must integrate privacy and security. Get it right, and your products, services, and experiences become and stay accessible. Get it wrong, and you increase risk, cost, and technical debt.

title: How to choose the right VPAT approach for your organization (and whether you should use AI to complete your ACR!)
partialText:
In this post, I’m going to discuss why accuracy matters for digital accessibility in an era of evolving global standards and increased regulatory scrutiny. I’ll explain where and how VPATs and ACRs fit into your accessibility strategies, and what you need to know before making any decisions about AI use.

title: Find Label in Name issues in every scan with Axe-core 4.14.0
partialText:
With our latest update, when you scan with Axe-core 4.14.0, you’ll now get a result for any control whose accessible name doesn't contain its visible label.

This Axe-core release also speeds up scans, makes fix instructions clearer, and begins support for EN 301 549 v4.1.1, the pending update to the European Union’s (EU) harmonized standard for accessibility requirements.

The post Find Label in Name issues in every scan with Axe-core 4.14.0 appeared first on Deque.

title: Debunking AI agent accessibility claims and solving AI alignment for accessibility
partialText:
There is a digital accessibility approach that gives us the best of both worlds: the reliability and predictability of rules-based testing and the velocity of AI-powered automation. By taking this approach, we can close the gap between presumed and actual accessibility.

title: How to test MCP Apps for accessibility, and why it matters
partialText:
MCP Apps are still new enough that whatever approaches we can establish now will be the ones that stick over the long term. Which means if we can get accessibility right at this stage, it will stay right as the ecosystem grows. This is how we can avoid introducing the same problems we've had to deal with across the rest of the web for so long.
